description: FOUND s504c (probed first, it reproduces).  Repro /home/bernt/pcl/.claude/worktrees/agent-a41c97e5832f266e1/scratch/s504c/probes/q10.pl + q10d.pl: q10.pl `$cnt="gc"; do "./q10d.pl"; do "./q10d.pl"; print "main: $cnt"`, q10d.pl `my $cnt; sub inc10 { ++$cnt } inc10(); print "inc10=", inc10(), "\n"; 1;`.  perl: inc10=2 / inc10=2 / main: gc.  s504c: inc10=2 / inc10=4 / main: gc (base b7ec0093 was worse: inc10=ge / gg, main: gg).  The decl `my $cnt;` lowers to a p-defcell whose init is guarded by boundp (define-once, right for BEGIN-stored values) and no run-time reset.  Fix shape: the RUN position of a no-initialiser promoted decl stores a fresh undef box unless a BEGIN in the unit wrote it (the read-only/BEGIN case of #2633 must keep working: b2.pl).
subject: A file-level `my $x;` with NO initialiser keeps its OLD value when the same unit runs twice (`do FILE` twice, or the same eval text twice): perl 2/2, PCL 2/4 -- the unit-unique cell is per TEXT, and the p-defcell decl does not reset it
